name: LEP Point 8 (DELPHI)
notes: Point number inferred from a CERN news article describing 'a miniature model of the underground cavern featuring the DELPHI and LHCb detectors', displayed at the LHCb exhibition at CERN's Point 8 (src:lep-cern-lhcb-exhibition-news, src:lep-cern-lhcb-experiment-page): the two detectors are stated to share the same cavern, and LHCb's own page and the voisins.cern Point 8 page both place LHCb at Point 8 / Ferney-Voltaire, so DELPHI is placed there too. No single fetched sentence states 'DELPHI was at Point 8' in so many words. (src:lep-cern-lhcb-experiment-page corroborates LHCb's own location at Ferney-Voltaire/Point 8.)

summary.plain: The underground cavern at Point 8 of the LEP ring, near the French town of Ferney-Voltaire, where the DELPHI detector recorded electron-positron collisions from 1989 to 2000. The same cavern now houses the LHCb experiment.
summary.technical: LEP interaction point 8, in Ferney-Voltaire (Ain, France); housed the DELPHI detector for the full LEP programme, later re-equipped for LHCb.
